Removes entries from the WAL file that have already been applied (based on
checkpoint).

This reduces WAL file size by keeping only unapplied entries.

When a scheduler daemon holds the object WAL open, standalone compaction can
orphan

file descriptors or corrupt state — this command refuses unless you pass
--force.

  Compact WAL file when scheduler daemon is stopped
  zqk system compact-wal
  JSON output for automation
  zqk system compact-wal --format json
  Force compaction even if scheduler appears running (unsafe)
  zqk system compact-wal --force

Usage:
  zqk system compact-wal [flags]

Flags:
      --columns string          Override column widths for table output (format: field:width)
      --force                   Allow compaction while the scheduler daemon appears to be running (unsafe; prefer stopping the daemon or letting the write-behind worker compact via TryCompactWAL)
  -f, --format string           Output format (table, json, jsonl, yaml, csv, json-rpc, stream, agent-prompt, semantic-link) (default "table")
      --ignore-scheduler-down   Ignore scheduler down warning/lockdown
  -o, --output string           Write output to file
  -q, --quiet                   Suppress non-essential output
      --timeout duration        Timeout for command execution (0 = auto-calculate)
  -v, --verbose                 Verbose output

Global Flags:
      --allow-degraded   Allow scheduler-dependent commands to run when scheduler daemon is not running
